title: Tally
summary: A local-first health and nutrition tracker for one person, with an AI coach.
description: Tally keeps a diary of what one person eats, how they train, fast and sleep, and what they notice about themselves, and a coach that reads it. Logging is meant to cost a photo, so the diary actually gets kept.

stories.as: someone tracking food, training and fasting
stories.want: to log a meal or a workout by taking a photo
stories.soThat: keeping a diary costs me seconds, not minutes

stories.want: my diary to have no server of its own
stories.soThat: it stays on my devices unless I send it somewhere

requirements.text: All data lives in a SQLite database on the user's devices, and Tally has no server of its own.

history.text: All data lives in a SQLite database on the user's devices; Tally has no server of its own.
history.reason: Version 1 said nothing of what does leave the device: captures and diary context go to OpenRouter, product names to Open Food Facts.

history.text: All data lives in a SQLite database on the user's devices; Tally has no server of its own, and data leaves a device only for the AI, food-lookup and Garmin services the user sets up.
history.reason: Version 2 held two promises; where data leaves a device is now TAL-4.

requirements.text: Release builds are produced for Android and for macOS.
The app has five tabs, in this order: Diary, Summary, Body, Coach, Settings.
Data leaves the vault's devices only for the AI, food-lookup and Garmin services the user sets up, and in exports the user makes.
